context.requirement_text:
Second half of ISS-0431/GH#835's fix for its own stated PRIMARY
surface, atop REQ-216's core module. Mirrors REQ-186/REQ-187's and
REQ-214/REQ-215's own "core module first, wiring requirement(s)
second, disjoint files" split precedent in this file.

TWO ADMISSION GATES, NOT ONE, because tenant identity is not known
until partway through `Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline`'s existing chain --
read in full (lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex): `Plug.Parsers` runs
first, then `assign_trace_id`, then `Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline`
(which itself resolves tenant identity via a DB read -- token
verification, tenant-by-realm/slug resolution, JIT provisioning --
i.e. AuthPipeline's OWN work already consumes a DB connection BEFORE
any tenant identity exists to gate on), then
`Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`, then `match`/`dispatch`. Given that
ordering, a single per-tenant-only gate cannot run early enough to
cover AuthPipeline's own connection use. Resolved as follows, stated
as an accepted, disclosed limitation rather than silently glossed
over (matching this project's own honesty convention for a limitation
that cannot be fully closed within one requirement's scope, e.g.
decision 0014's own disclosed WASM native-crash gap):

1. GLOBAL gate, mounted FIRST in the chain -- before `Plug.Parsers`,
so a request rejected for lack of capacity is rejected before any
body-parsing work is spent on it. Calls
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire(:global)`. Covers AuthPipeline's own
connection use (the gap named above) because it runs before
AuthPipeline and gates ALL downstream DB-connection-holding work,
auth included.
2. PER-TENANT gate, mounted immediately AFTER `Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline`
(tenant identity now resolved into `conn.assigns.auth_context.tenant_id`)
and BEFORE `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`/`match`/`dispatch`. Calls
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire({:tenant, schema_name})`, resolving
`schema_name` the same way `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus` and
`Letflow.Scheduler.Poller` already do (tenant-id -> schema-name
resolution already exists in this codebase; reuse it, do not
re-derive). Covers TenantStatus's own DB lookup and every sub-router's
dispatch work -- the dominant share of connection-holding time per
REQ-056/ISS-0431's own round-trip profiling.
DISCLOSED LIMITATION: AuthPipeline's own DB work (steps 1-4 of its
moduledoc) is covered by the global gate only, not a per-tenant one,
because tenant identity does not exist yet at that point in the
chain. This is accepted, not silently omitted -- state it in this
plug's own moduledoc.
3. Both gates: on `{:error, :capacity}`, respond immediately (halt the
plug chain, no further plugs run) via
`Letflow.Api.Response.service_unavailable/2` (REQ-066, ALREADY
EXISTING -- do not add a new response helper), with the
`Retry-After` header set explicitly on the conn first (matching
`Response.rate_limited/2`'s own documented "caller sets Retry-After"
convention) to a fixed, configured seconds value (config, default 1)
-- NOT a computed estimate, since this admission mechanism has no
queueing/backoff-timing model to estimate from (a fixed short value
matching `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`'s own existing `@retry_after_seconds
"30"` precedent's SHAPE, though the specific number here is
independently justified: admission rejection is a near-instant
decision with no wait queue behind it, unlike TenantStatus's
migration-in-progress case, so a MUCH shorter retry-after is
appropriate -- state this reasoning in the plug's moduledoc rather
than copying TenantStatus's 30-second value uncritically).
4. On success at BOTH gates: the plug stores both `admission_ref()`s
in `conn.assigns` and registers a `Plug.Conn.register_before_send/2`
(or equivalent, matching how this codebase already threads
request-scoped cleanup -- state which mechanism is chosen and why) or
calls `Letflow.Admission.release/1` for both refs when the response is
sent, so an admitted request's slot is freed exactly once, on every
response path including a request that raises inside a downstream
plug or router (verified in the acceptance criteria below).
NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no change to REQ-216's core semaphore logic;
no change to `Letflow.Plugs.RateLimit` (still deferred, unmounted,
unrelated mechanism); no Poller wiring (REQ-218); no tier-weighted
per-tenant caps (REQ-216's own recorded open question).

result.summary:
Independently re-derived REQ-217 as done. Read full handoff chain step-00..step-09 and the actual shipped code (lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex, lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex) and tests (test/letflow/plugs/admission_test.exs, test/letflow/plugs/admission_pipeline_test.exs), not any prior agent's narrative.

INDEPENDENT TEST RE-RUNS (both foreground, both waited out synchronously, no backgrounding/notification-wait):
1. scripts/test_parallel.sh (TEST_PARALLEL_N=8): combined 3087 tests, 6 properties, 2 failures (3091/3093 passed). Both failures isolated to partition 6, both in Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckToolchainTest ('a matching rust pin reports OK...' and 'a mismatched rust pin reports a MISMATCH row...'), both raising Erlang :enoent from System.cmd("rustc", ...). Confirmed directly on this host: `which rustc` exits 1 (no rustc installed) -- the documented pre-existing toolchain-flake category, structurally unrelated to this branch. Zero failures in admission_test.exs or admission_pipeline_test.exs across all 8 partitions (grepped every partition log for Admission-related failure lines; the one hit found was an unrelated teardown info-log line, not a failure). git diff --stat main...HEAD -- lib/ shows exactly 3 files changed (design doc, admission.ex, api_pipeline.ex) -- this run's failure set does not touch either changed lib/ file, structurally ruling out a regression per this project's own failure-attribution rule. This run's failure SET (2, both rustc) differs from TEST-RUNNER's own prior full run (16, 2 rustc + 14 flaky) and from TEST-DESIGNER's own prior run (2, both rustc) -- consistent with the already-documented timing-dependent flakiness of the other 14 under full concurrent load, not evidence of anything new.
2. mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force: clean ('Compiling 184 files (.ex)' / 'Generated letflow app', no warnings, no errors).
3. mix letflow.check.test (single-process, the stricter check per this role's own mandate -- NOT skipped): 'Finished in 1552.0 seconds ... Result: 3094/3096 passed (6/6 properties, 3088/3090 tests), 10 excluded. Failed: 2 tests' -- both the same rust-pin/rustc-ENOENT pair as above (confirmed by reading both failure headers directly: 'a matching rust pin reports OK...' / 'a mismatched rust pin reports a MISMATCH row...', Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckToolchainTest). Grepped the full ~39MB captured output for the fixed substring 'default values for the optional arguments' (the exact ISS-0069 dead-default-argument signature this task exists to catch) -- zero matches. The task's own wrapper still reports 'FAILED -- underlying mix test run exited 2' because mix test itself exited 2 on the 2 real (but pre-existing, environmental) rustc failures; that is expected given no rustc on this host and is not a REQ-217 regression.

AC-BY-AC RE-VERIFICATION (pulled fresh from docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-217 entry, checked against actual code/tests, not any prior summary):
AC1 (global cap 0 -> every request 503+Retry-After, Plug.Parsers never runs, oversized body still 503 not 413): api_pipeline.ex line 86 mounts `plug(Letflow.Plugs.Admission, pool: :global)` as the literal first plug, before Plug.Parsers (line 112). admission_pipeline_test.exs describe 'AC1' has both the plain-503 test and the oversized-body-still-503-not-413 test. PASS.
AC2 (per-tenant cap 0 for tenant A -> 503, tenant B same global cap -> succeeds, same test): admission_pipeline_test.exs describe 'AC2' test exhausts tenant A's fair share directly against the real Letflow.Admission singleton, asserts tenant A 503+Retry-After and tenant B (probed first into the fair-share divisor) reaches 404 (non-503) in the same test. PASS.
AC3 (admitted request completing normally releases both refs exactly once, verified by exhausting cap then a subsequent request succeeding): admission_pipeline_test.exs describe 'AC3' runs cap=1 (post-§10.1-fix minimum) two sequential requests, both non-503/404. PASS.
AC4 (downstream handler raise still releases both refs): admission_pipeline_test.exs describe 'AC4' forces an Ecto.Query.CastError inside Letflow.Routers.Identity's matched route handler (Plug.Conn.WrapperError), asserts a follow-up request at cap=1 still gets 200 -- only possible if both refs were released by Mechanism B (handle_errors/2 -> release_pending_refs/0). Code: api_pipeline.ex's `use Plug.ErrorHandler` + handle_errors/2 (lines 180-184) delegates to Letflow.Plugs.Admission.release_pending_refs/0, which drains and releases every ref in the process-dictionary list (admission.ex lines 259-267). PASS.
AC5 (503 body shape matches Letflow.Api.Response.service_unavailable/2's existing Error.service_unavailable/1 shape exactly, compared against test/letflow/api/error_test.exs's existing expected shape): admission_test.exs describe 'AC5' (lines 76+) asserts the same four RFC 9457 fields via the same constructor. admission.ex's reject/2 (lines 240-245) calls Response.service_unavailable/2 with no ad hoc body -- no new response helper was added, matching the requirement's explicit prohibition. PASS.
AC6 (chain order: global admission first before Plug.Parsers; per-tenant admission after AuthPipeline, before TenantStatus): read api_pipeline.ex directly myself -- line 86 global, line 112 Plug.Parsers, line 119 AuthPipeline, line 128 :release_global_admission, line 133 tenant admission, line 135 TenantStatus. Order confirmed exactly as required. admission_pipeline_test.exs's own 'AC6' describe block also asserts this via byte-offset comparison of the source file. PASS.
AC7 (mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted): both independently re-run above by me, real output quoted; the only failures are the pre-existing, host-specific rustc-ENOENT gap, structurally unrelated to any file this branch touches. PASS (with the same documented, pre-existing environmental caveat every prior REQ-216/REQ-217 gate has already carried).

SECTION 10 (SECURITY-REVIEWER's own found-and-fixed double-global-consumption defect) INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED PRESENT IN SHIPPED CODE: api_pipeline.ex line 128 mounts `plug(:release_global_admission)` between AuthPipeline (line 119) and the tenant admission mount (line 133); the private wrapper (line 167) delegates to Letflow.Plugs.Admission.release_global_ref/1 (admission.ex lines 219-237), which releases the global gate's already-held ref, removes it from the process-dictionary list via List.delete/2 (not a full clear -- leaves the tenant ref, added later, untouched), and re-assigns the conn key to nil. admission_pipeline_test.exs's dedicated 'REQ-217 rework (design doc §10.1)' describe block has two tests directly re-deriving this: global_cap==1 admits one full request end to end (would have needed cap==2 under the pre-fix double-consumption bug), and a direct probe immediately after response completion confirming the global counter is back to fully free. Both read and independently verified PASS.

STALENESS CHECK: docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-217 entry still reads `status: in_progress` -- accurate, matches the 'started' event (2026-09-03T02:45:00Z, no 'done' event yet) at the tail of docs/status/requirement_status.v8.yaml. Ready for DOC-UPDATER to flip. No docs/migration/decisions/ record contradicted (design doc's §10.1 rework and disclosed AuthPipeline-DB-work limitation are both consistent with decision 0014's own disclosed-limitation precedent, which the requirement text itself cites). This is a WF-02 single-requirement run, not a stage gate, so no docs/migration/stage-N-*.md sign-off section is required at this step.
